scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The two departments have been CUT OFF from each
other!! From the department head's machine, none of the computers in the other
department answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's just the other
one that's gone. Something that joins the two departments must be wrong, but I
don't know what. Could someone look at it and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested inter-department connectivity end-to-end and everything is currently healthy. From the CS department head’s PC (cs_hod 192.168.2.2), pings to the IT department head (it_hod 192.168.1.2) and to all IT lab hosts (it_lab1–it_lab4, 192.168.1.3–1.6) succeed with 0% loss. From the IT department head’s PC (it_hod 192.168.1.2), pings to CS lab hosts (cs_lab1–cs_lab4, 192.168.2.3–2.6) also succeed with 0% loss. This confirms bidirectional reachability between the two departments.

Router0, which joins the CS and IT LANs, has both department-facing interfaces up (eth0=192.168.1.1, eth1=192.168.2.1) and is routing correctly; hosts in each department have proper defaults (cs_hod via 192.168.2.1, it_hod via 192.168.1.1). Router0’s routing table also shows learned routes for other campus subnets, indicating its control plane is functioning.

Mechanism-wise, if a joining device were down or misconfigured (e.g., gateway off, interface down, ACL), cross-subnet pings would fail. Since they do not, there is no active fault isolating the departments. The symptom described cannot be reproduced now.

Root cause: No network fault found; likely a transient condition (momentary routing/host issue) or a misidentified endpoint during the report.

Corrective fix: No changes required. Recommend the users retry, verify target IPs/hostnames, and if the issue recurs intermittently, capture times and we’ll monitor router0 and the two switches (switch0/switch1) during that window for flaps or errors.
